Relocation model for x64/x86 (SimpleRelocation only). Mirrors runtime/src/relocations.rs.

Types

RelocationKind = enum
  rkRelative = 0,           ## PC-relative, no adjust on move
  rkAbsToRel = 1,           ## absolute -> relative, needs adjust
  rkRelToAbs = 2,           ## relative -> absolute, needs adjust
  rkAbsolute = 3             ## absolute, no adjust
RelocationSize = enum
  rsByte = 1, rsWord = 2, rsDWord = 4, rsQWord = 8
SimpleRelocation = object
  kind*: RelocationKind
  size*: RelocationSize
  arch*: int8 ## -1 for plain x64/x86 relocations, else an AArch64 arch-specific
              ## encoding id (mirrors dynasm-rs Aarch64RelocationEncoding):
              ## 0=B, 1=BCOND, 2=ADR, 3=ADRP, 4=TBZ.

Consts

AarchAdr = 2
adr: split 21 bit, byte aligned 
AarchAdrp = 3
adrp: split 21 bit, 4096-byte aligned 
AarchB = 0
b, bl: 26 bits, dword aligned 
AarchBCond = 1
b.cond, cbz, cbnz, ldr literal: 19 bits, dword aligned 
AarchTbz = 4
tbz, tbnz: 14 bits, dword aligned 
EncByte = 0
EncDWord = 2
EncQWord = 3
EncWord = 1

proc encodeAarchReloc(id: int): uint8 {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Pack an AArch64 arch-specific relocation for macro emission. Plain x64/x86 codes always have low 6 bits 0..3, so ids live at 4..8 with zero kind bits (mirrors how rs keeps arch codes disjoint from the simple ones). Addition, not OR: 0x04|4 would collapse back to 0x04 and mistarget TBZ as B.
